sanskrit: visṛjya ca mahābāhur ṛkṣavānararākṣasān bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito rāmaḥ pramumoda sukhī sukham
english: Having dismissed the bears, monkeys, and rākṣasas, the mighty-armed Rāma, together with his brothers, rejoiced in perfect happiness.

sanskrit: athāparāhṇasamaye bhrātṛbhiḥ saha rāghavaḥ śuśrāva madhurāṃ vāṇīm antarikṣāt prabhāṣitām
english: Then, in the afternoon, Rāghava along with his brothers heard a sweet voice speaking down from the sky.

sanskrit: saumya rāma nirīkṣasva saumyena vadanena mām kailāsaśikharāt prāptaṃ viddhi māṃ puṣkaraṃ prabho
english: "Gentle Rāma, look upon me with your gracious countenance. Know me, O lord, as Puṣpaka, arrived from the peak of Kailāsa.

sanskrit: tava śāsanam ājñāya gato 'smi dhanadaṃ prati upasthātuṃ naraśreṣṭha sa ca māṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: "Following your command, O best of men, I went to wait upon Dhanada, the lord of wealth, and he spoke to me thus.

sanskrit: nirjitas tvaṃ narendreṇa rāghaveṇa mahātmanā nihatya yudhi durdharṣaṃ rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam
english: "'You have been won back by the king of men, the great-souled Rāghava, who slew in battle the terrible Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: mamāpi paramā prītir hate tasmin durātmani rāvaṇe sagaṇe saumya saputrāmātyabāndhave
english: "'My own supreme delight, O gentle one, is in the slaying of that wicked Rāvaṇa together with his troops, his sons, ministers, and kinsmen.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ rāmeṇa laṅkāyāṃ nirjitaḥ paramātmanā vaha saumya tam eva tvam aham ājñāpayāmi te
english: "'You who were won in Laṅkā by the supremely noble Rāma — O gentle one, serve him alone: this I command you.

sanskrit: eṣa me paramaḥ kāmo yat tvaṃ rāghavanandanam vaher lokasya saṃyānaṃ gacchasva vigatajvaraḥ
english: "'This is my highest wish: that you carry Rāghava, the joy of the world, wherever he desires. Go now, free from all care."

sanskrit: tacchāsanam ahaṃ jñātvā dhanadasya mahātmanaḥ tvatsakāśaṃ punaḥ prāptaḥ sa evaṃ pratigṛhṇa mām
english: "Having learnt this command of the great-souled lord of wealth, I have come again to your presence. Accept me thus, O lord."

sanskrit: bāḍham ity eva kākutsthaḥ puṣpakaṃ samapūjayat lājākṣataiś ca puṣpaiś ca gandhaiś ca susugandhibhiḥ
english: "So be it" — with these words the scion of Kakutstha duly honoured Puṣpaka with fried grain, unbroken rice, flowers, and fragrant perfumes.

sanskrit: gamyatāṃ ca yathākāmam āgacches tvaṃ yadā smare evam astv iti rāmeṇa visṛṣṭaḥ puṣpakaḥ punaḥ abhipretāṃ diśaṃ prāyāt puṣpakaḥ puṣpabhūṣitaḥ
english: "Go wherever you please, and return when I recall you" — thus dismissed by Rāma, Puṣpaka departed once more, adorned with blossoms, in the direction of its desire.

sanskrit: evam antarhite tasmin puṣpake vividhātmani bharataḥ prāñjalir vākyam uvāca raghunandanam
english: When that wondrous Puṣpaka had disappeared from sight, Bharata, with joined palms, spoke these words to the delight of the Raghus.

sanskrit: atyadbhutāni dṛśyante tvayi rājyaṃ praśāsati amānuṣāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ vyāhṛtāni muhur muhuḥ
english: "Exceedingly marvellous things appear while you govern the kingdom — the utterances of non-human beings are heard again and again.

sanskrit: anāmayāc ca martyānāṃ sāgro māso gato hy ayam jīrṇānām api sattvānāṃ mṛtyur nāyāti rāghava
english: "And from freedom from disease among mortals — this full month has now passed, O Rāghava, and even old creatures have not met with death.

sanskrit: putrān nāryaḥ prasūyante vapuṣmantaś ca mānavāḥ harṣaś cābhyadhiko rājañ janasya puravāsinaḥ
english: "Women give birth to fine sons, and men are handsome of form; and the joy of the city-dwelling people is extraordinarily great, O king.

sanskrit: kāle ca vāsavo varṣaṃ pātayaty amṛtopamam vāyavaś cāpi vāyante sparśavantaḥ sukhapradāḥ
english: "Indra showers rain in season, rain akin to nectar, and breezes blow that are pleasant to the touch and bestow comfort.

sanskrit: īdṛśo naś ciraṃ rājā bhavatv iti nareśvara kathayanti pure paurā janā janapadeṣu ca
english: "'May such a king be ours for long' — so speak the citizens in the city, O lord of men, and the people in the countryside.

sanskrit: etā vācaḥ sumadhurā bharatena samīritāḥ śrutvā rāmo mudā yuktaḥ pramumoda sukhī sukham
english: Having heard these exceedingly sweet words uttered by Bharata, Rāma, filled with joy, rejoiced in utter happiness.

sanskrit: sa visṛjya tato rāmaḥ puṣpakaṃ hemabhūṣitam praviveśa mahābāhur aśokavanikāṃ tadā
english: Then Rāma, the mighty-armed, having dismissed the gold-adorned Puṣpaka, entered the Aśoka grove.

sanskrit: candanāgarucūtaiś ca tuṅgakāleyakair api devadāruvanaiś cāpi samantād upaśobhitām
english: It was beautified on all sides with sandalwood, agaru, mango, tall kāleyaka, and forests of devadāru trees.

sanskrit: priyaṅgubhiḥ kadambaiś ca tathā kurabakair api jambūbhiḥ pāṭalībhiś ca kovidāraiś ca saṃvṛtām
english: It was covered with priyaṅgu, kadamba, kurabaka, jambū, pāṭalī, and kovidāra trees.

sanskrit: sarvadā kusumai ramyaiḥ phalavadbhir manoramaiḥ cārupallavapuṣpāḍhyair mattabhramarasaṃkulaiḥ
english: At all times it was lovely with beautiful flowers, laden with fruits, delightful, rich with charming shoots and blossoms, and thronged with maddened bees.

sanskrit: kokilair bhṛṅgarājaiś ca nānāvarṇaiś ca pakṣibhiḥ śobhitāṃ śataśaś citraiś cūtavṛkṣāvataṃsakaiḥ
english: It was adorned with cuckoos, bhṛṅgarājas, birds of many colours, and hundreds of variegated mango trees as its ornaments.

sanskrit: śātakumbhanibhāḥ ke cit ke cid agniśikhopamāḥ nīlāñjananibhāś cānye bhānti tatra sma pādapāḥ
english: There the trees shone — some resembling refined gold, some like tongues of fire, and others like blue collyrium.

sanskrit: dīrghikā vividhākārāḥ pūrṇāḥ paramavāriṇā mahārhamaṇisopānasphaṭikāntarakuṭṭimāḥ
english: There were ponds of various forms, filled with the finest water, with steps of precious gems and floors inlaid with crystal.

sanskrit: phullapadmotpalavanāś cakravākopaśobhitāḥ prākārair vividhākāraiḥ śobhitāś ca śilātalaiḥ
english: They were adorned with groves of blooming lotuses and blue water-lilies, graced by cakravāka birds, and beautified by enclosures of various forms and stone pavements.

sanskrit: tatra tatra vanoddeśe vaidūryamaṇisaṃnibhaiḥ śādvalaiḥ paramopetāḥ puṣpitadrumasaṃyutāḥ
english: Here and there in the woodland's expanse were lawns resembling vaidūrya gems, adorned most excellently, set about with flowering trees.

sanskrit: nandanaṃ hi yathendrasya brāhmaṃ caitrarathaṃ yathā tathārūpaṃ hi rāmasya kānanaṃ tan niveśitam
english: Rāma's grove had been laid out to resemble Indra's Nandana, and likewise Brahmā's Caitraratha garden.

sanskrit: bahvāsanagṛhopetāṃ latāgṛhasamāvṛtām aśokavanikāṃ sphītāṃ praviśya raghunandanaḥ
english: Entering that flourishing Aśoka grove — abounding in pavilions and arbours, enveloped with bowers of creepers — the delight of the Raghus took his seat.

sanskrit: āsane tu śubhākāre puṣpastabakabhūṣite kuthāstaraṇasaṃvīte rāmaḥ saṃniṣasāda ha
english: Rāma seated himself upon a fine-formed seat adorned with clusters of flowers and spread with a woollen coverlet.

sanskrit: sītāṃ saṃgṛhya bāhubhyāṃ madhumaireyam uttamam pāyayām āsa kākutsthaḥ śacīm indro yathāmṛtam
english: Taking Sītā into his arms, the scion of Kakutstha gave her the finest sweet wine to drink, as Indra gives nectar to Śacī.

sanskrit: māṃsāni ca vicitrāṇi phalāni vividhāni ca rāmasyābhyavahārārthaṃ kiṃkarās tūrṇam āharan
english: Attendants quickly brought diverse kinds of meat and various fruits for Rāma's enjoyment.

sanskrit: upanṛtyanti rājānaṃ nṛtyagītaviśāradāḥ bālāś ca rūpavatyaś ca striyaḥ pānavaśaṃ gatāḥ
english: Young and beautiful women skilled in dance and song danced before the king, yielding to the sway of wine.

sanskrit: evaṃ rāmo mudā yuktaḥ sītāṃ surucirānanām ramayām āsa vaidehīm ahany ahani devavat
english: Thus Rāma, filled with joy, delighted Vaidehī — the daughter of Videha, whose face was most lovely — day after day, in the manner of a god.

sanskrit: tathā tu ramamāṇasya tasyaivaṃ śiśiraḥ śubhaḥ atyakrāman narendrasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: While the great-souled king of men, Rāghava, was thus taking his pleasure, the lovely cool season passed by.

sanskrit: pūrvāhṇe paurakṛtyāni kṛtvā dharmeṇa dharmavit śeṣaṃ divasabhāgārdham antaḥpuragato 'bhavat
english: In the forenoon, having discharged his civic duties righteously, the knower of dharma would spend the remaining half of the day's portion within the inner apartments.

sanskrit: sītā ca devakāryāṇi kṛtvā paurvāhṇikāni tu śvaśrūṇām aviśeṣeṇa sarvāsāṃ prāñjaliḥ sthitā
english: And Sītā, having performed her morning religious observances, would stand with joined palms before all her mothers-in-law without distinction.

sanskrit: tato rāmam upāgacchad vicitrabahubhūṣaṇā triviṣṭape sahasrākṣam upaviṣṭaṃ yathā śacī
english: Then she would come to Rāma adorned with varied and manifold ornaments, as Śacī comes to the thousand-eyed Indra seated in heaven.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu rāghavaḥ patnīṃ kalyāṇena samanvitām praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe sādhu sādhv iti cābravīt
english: Seeing his wife endowed with every auspicious quality, Rāghava was filled with incomparable delight and said, "Well done, well done."

sanskrit: apatyalābho vaidehi mamāyaṃ samupasthitaḥ kim icchasi hi tad brūhi kaḥ kāmaḥ kriyatāṃ tava
english: "O Vaidehī, the gaining of offspring is now at hand for me. Tell me what you desire — what is your wish? Let it be done for you."

sanskrit: prahasantī tu vaidehī rāmaṃ vākyam athābravīt tapovanāni puṇyāni draṣṭum icchāmi rāghava
english: Then Vaidehī, smiling gently, spoke these words to Rāma: "I desire to see the holy forest hermitages, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: gaṅgātīre niviṣṭāni ṛṣīṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām phalamūlāśināṃ vīra pādamūleṣu vartitum
english: "Those that are established on the banks of the Gaṅgā, belonging to the sages who perform meritorious deeds and live on fruits and roots — O hero, to dwell at the feet of such sages.

sanskrit: eṣa me paramaḥ kāmo yan mūlaphalabhojiṣu apy ekarātraṃ kākutstha vaseyaṃ puṇyaśāliṣu
english: "This is my supreme desire — O scion of Kakutstha, that I might dwell even for a single night among those meritorious ones who live on roots and fruits."

sanskrit: tatheti ca pratijñātaṃ rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā visrabdhā bhava vaidehi śvo gamiṣyasy asaṃśayam
english: "So be it" — this was promised by Rāma of untiring deeds. "Be assured, O Vaidehī — you will go tomorrow, without doubt."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu kākutstho maithilīṃ janakātmajām madhyakakṣāntaraṃ rāmo nirjagāma suhṛdvṛtaḥ
english: Having spoken thus to Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, Rāma, the scion of Kakutstha, went out into the middle courtyard surrounded by his friends.

sanskrit: tatropaviṣṭaṃ rājānam upāsante vicakṣaṇāḥ kathānāṃ bahurūpāṇāṃ hāsyakārāḥ samantataḥ
english: There, skilled raconteurs of many kinds of stories — men who provoke laughter — attended upon the king as he sat, on all sides.

sanskrit: vijayo madhumattaś ca kāśyapaḥ piṅgalaḥ kuśaḥ surājiḥ kāliyo bhadro dantavakraḥ samāgadhaḥ
english: Vijaya, Madhumatta, Kāśyapa, Piṅgala, Kuśa, Surāji, Kāliya, Bhadra, Dantavakra, and Samāgadha —

sanskrit: ete kathā bahuvidhā parihāsasamanvitāḥ kathayanti sma saṃhṛṣṭā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: — these men joyfully narrated to the great-souled Rāghava stories of many kinds, full of jests and amusing tales.

sanskrit: tataḥ kathāyāṃ kasyāṃ cid rāghavaḥ samabhāṣata kāḥ kathā nagare bhadra vartante viṣayeṣu ca
english: Then, in the course of some conversation, Rāghava asked: "What stories, O Bhadra, are circulating in the city and in the countryside?

sanskrit: mām āśritāni kāny āhuḥ paurajānapadā janāḥ kiṃ ca sītāṃ samāśritya bharataṃ kiṃ nu lakṣmaṇam
english: "What do the townspeople and country folk say regarding me? And what regarding Sītā, and what regarding Bharata, and what of Lakṣmaṇa?

sanskrit: kiṃ nu śatrughnam āśritya kaikeyīṃ mātaraṃ ca me vaktavyatāṃ ca rājāno nave rājye vrajanti hi
english: "And what regarding Śatrughna, and my mother Kaikeyī? For kings in a new reign do become subjects of public speech."

sanskrit: evam ukte tu rāmeṇa bhadraḥ prāñjalir abravīt sthitāḥ kathāḥ śubhā rājan vartante puravāsinām
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Bhadra, with joined palms, replied: "Auspicious stories, O king, circulate among the city-dwellers —

sanskrit: ayaṃ tu vijayaḥ saumya daśagrīvavadhāśritaḥ bhūyiṣṭhaṃ svapure pauraiḥ kathyate puruṣarṣabha
english: "— but this victory of yours, O gentle one, pertaining to the slaying of the ten-necked one, is what is talked of most by the citizens in the city, O bull among men.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu bhadreṇa rāghavo vākyam abravīt kathayasva yathātathyaṃ sarvaṃ niravaśeṣataḥ
english: Thus addressed by Bhadra, Rāghava spoke: "Tell me everything truthfully and completely, holding nothing back.

sanskrit: śubhāśubhāni vākyāni yāny āhuḥ puravāsinaḥ śrutvedānīṃ śubhaṃ kuryāṃ na kuryām aśubhāni ca
english: "The words — both good and ill — that the city-dwellers speak: having heard them now, I shall act on what is good and refrain from what is ill.

sanskrit: kathayasva ca visrabdho nirbhayo vigatajvaraḥ kathayante yathā paurā janā janapadeṣu ca
english: "Speak openly, without fear, free from all anxiety, exactly as the citizens speak, and as the people speak in the countryside."

sanskrit: rāghaveṇaivam uktas tu bhadraḥ suruciraṃ vacaḥ pratyuvāca mahābāhuṃ prāñjaliḥ susamāhitaḥ
english: Thus spoken to by Rāghava, Bhadra, standing with joined palms and fully composed, replied to the mighty-armed king with these well-chosen words:

sanskrit: śṛṇu rājan yathā paurāḥ kathayanti śubhāśubham catvarāpaṇarathyāsu vaneṣūpavaneṣu ca
english: "Hear, O king, how the citizens speak — both good and ill — at crossroads, in markets, on the streets, in forests and in gardens.

sanskrit: duṣkaraṃ kṛtavān rāmaḥ samudre setubandhanam akṛtaṃ pūrvakaiḥ kaiś cid devair api sadānavaiḥ
english: "'Rāma accomplished the formidable feat of building a bridge across the ocean — something never done before by any predecessors, not even by gods or dānavas.

sanskrit: rāvaṇaś ca durādharṣo hataḥ sabalavāhanaḥ vānarāś ca vaśaṃ nītā ṛkṣāś ca saha rākṣasaiḥ
english: "'And the terrible Rāvaṇa was slain together with his army and forces; monkeys were brought to submission, and bears together with rākṣasas.

sanskrit: hatvā ca rāvaṇaṃ yuddhe sītām āhṛtya rāghavaḥ amarṣaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā svaveśma punar ānayat
english: "'Having slain Rāvaṇa in battle and recovered Sītā, Rāghava set his anger aside and brought her back to his own home.

sanskrit: kīdṛśaṃ hṛdaye tasya sītāsaṃbhogajaṃ sukham aṅkam āropya hi purā rāvaṇena balād dhṛtām
english: "'What kind of pleasure in his heart can there be from enjoying Sītā — she who was formerly seized by force and placed in Rāvaṇa's lap?

sanskrit: laṅkām api punar nītām aśokavanikāṃ gatām rakṣasāṃ vaśam āpannāṃ kathaṃ rāmo na kutsate
english: "'She who was carried away again to Laṅkā, who went to the Aśoka grove, who fell under the power of the rākṣasas — how is it that Rāma does not reject her?

sanskrit: asmākam api dāreṣu sahanīyaṃ bhaviṣyati yathā hi kurute rājā prajā tam anuvartate
english: "'This will become something to be tolerated in our own wives as well — for as the king does, so the subjects follow.'

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhā vāco vadanti puravāsinaḥ nagareṣu ca sarveṣu rājañ janapadeṣu ca
english: "Thus do the city-dwellers speak in many ways, O king, in all the cities and throughout the countryside."

sanskrit: tasyaitad bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā rāghavaḥ paramārtavat uvāca sarvān suhṛdaḥ katham etan nivedyatām
english: Hearing these words of his, Rāghava, in the deepest anguish, said to all his friends: "How shall this be conveyed?"

sanskrit: sarve tu śirasā bhūmāv abhivādya praṇamya ca pratyūcū rāghavaṃ dīnam evam etan na saṃśayaḥ
english: But all of them, bowing low to the ground with their heads and prostrating themselves, replied to the grief-stricken Rāghava: "It is even so, without doubt."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vākyaṃ kākutsthaḥ sarveṣāṃ samudīritam visarjayām āsa tadā sarvāṃs tāñ śatrutāpanaḥ
english: Having heard the words uttered by all of them, the scion of Kakutstha, the tormentor of enemies, then dismissed them all.
